title: Apple Posts Record India Revenue as Mac and Services Hit Highs
excerpt: Apple's fiscal fourth quarter brought an all-time India revenue record, a September-quarter high for Indian iPhone upgraders, and global revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year.
body:
• Apple reported an all-time revenue record in India for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter ended September 26, with Mac and Services revenue also hitting all-time highs in the country, executives said on the earnings call.
  • Global revenue rose 12 percent year over year to $114.5 billion; net profit rose 11.8 percent to $30.7 billion and diluted EPS rose 14 percent to $2.10, including a $0.05 benefit from tariff refunds.
  • iPhone revenue rose 17 percent to $57.6 billion, Mac rose 24 percent to $10.8 billion and Services rose 10 percent to a record $31.6 billion; iPad and wearables revenue fell.
  • Apple guided December-quarter revenue growth of 7 to 10 percent year over year — guidance, not a result — and declared a $0.27 dividend payable November 16 to shareholders of record on November 12.

Apple reported an all-time revenue record in India in its fiscal fourth quarter, with its iPhone business setting a September-quarter revenue record in the country and Mac and services revenue reaching new highs there. The India results, described by executives on the earnings call and reported by Inc42, came as the company posted September-quarter records globally for the quarter ended September 26, 2026.

"We also set September quarter revenue records in both developed and emerging markets, in addition to an all-time record in India."

— John Ternus, Apple CEO, on the earnings call

In its official results release, Apple reported quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year. Company gross margin was 47.9 percent, including a favourable impact of approximately one percentage point from tariff refunds. Diluted earnings per share was $2.10, up 14 percent year over year, including a $0.05 favourable impact from tariff refunds. Consolidated net profit increased 11.8 percent to $30.7 billion, Inc42 reported. Apple did not publish a separate dollar figure for India in the release or in the call coverage.

Where the growth came from

Global iPhone revenue rose 17 percent year over year to $57.6 billion. Alongside India, the company recorded September-quarter highs for iPhone upgraders globally, in the US and in mainland China, and India itself set a September-quarter high for iPhone upgraders, CEO John Ternus said. Citing a recent Worldpanel survey, CFO Kevan Parekh said iPhone was among the top-selling smartphone models in India, the US, urban China, the UK, Germany, Australia and Japan.

Mac revenue increased 24 percent year over year to $10.8 billion globally. "We saw double-digit growth in both developed and emerging markets, with all-time records in markets like India and Southeast Asia," Parekh said. Apple also recorded a September-quarter high for customers buying a Mac for the first time. Services posted record global revenue of $31.6 billion, up 10 percent year over year, with all-time highs across most markets it tracks, including India and Latin America.

The weaker lines were smaller. Overall products revenue rose 12 percent to $82.9 billion, but iPad revenue declined 10 percent to $6.2 billion and wearables, home and accessories revenue fell 8 percent to $8.3 billion, Inc42 reported. For the full fiscal year 2026, revenue increased 15 percent to $478.8 billion — what Ternus called the company's best fiscal year ever.

Apple Pay extends the India services story

Apple expanded its services offering in India with the launch of Apple Pay on September 30, with Axis Bank as its first banking partner, Inc42 reported. The service supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards across iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch in apps, online and at contactless-enabled stores; Mac support is expected to follow and RuPay cards are not supported at launch. Apple said actual card numbers are neither stored on devices or its servers nor shared with merchants.

What to watch next

Apple expects December-quarter revenue to grow 7 to 10 percent year over year, which would take quarterly revenue to a new high — a company expectation reported by Inc42, not a reported result. Cost pressure is the counterweight: The Hindu BusinessLine reported management expecting December-quarter gross margin of 45 to 46 percent, reflecting higher memory costs and the cost of ramping Siri AI, with Ternus calling current memory pricing unprecedented. The board declared a cash dividend of $0.27 per share, payable November 16, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 12, according to the company's release.
